liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Main Ten** (1 review): Audience clapping during The Main Ten is enjoyed [15]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): Reviewer says the energy really kicks in at Good Lovin'; starting the listen there is suggested [8]
- **Alligator** (1 review): Searing guitar leads come in the jam out of Alligator, with the crowd getting into it; Garcia's guitar pops and connects over tribal rhythms in that jam, an intimate yet not quiet moment [5]
- **Goin' Down the Road Feeling Bad** (1 review): Reviewer says the closing jam alone would have made the night worthwhile [9]
- **Mountain Jam** (1 review): Reviewer recalled this as the show with the Mountain Jam and focused on the fourth disc, where the heat is [13]
- The jams are described as tremendously powerful [6]

## The recordings

- **gd70-11-06.aud.warner.17183.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 50 songs; 280 min; rated 4.15/5 by 26 [1]. Said about its sound: Described as a very good audience tape, though EQ adjustment is recommended; Audience recording judged quite unlistenable, though the performance deserves higher marks; Recording is barely listenable; reviewer suggests finding a better copy [8][10][11][14][15]
- **gd70-11-06.d3new.hanno.19922.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 14 songs; 78 min; rated 3.6/5 by 5 [3]
- **gd1970-11-06.aud.weinberg.moore-berger.119818.flac16**: audience recording; 8 songs; 35 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [4]
- **gd1970-11-06.aud.evans.3338.sbefail.shnf**: audience recording; 35 songs; 211 min; rated 4.2/5 by 10 [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended as their first official Dead show, taken by a brother; they taped only the acoustic set on a portable [9]
- Includes a soundcheck of Uncle John's Band, Candyman and Attics of My Life, called a rarity [12]
- Acoustic set runs through the first 1:50 of El Paso, followed by the electric set [1]
- The Dead played one show per night at the Capitol Theater, Thursday to Sunday, November 5-8, 1970 [2]
- Village Voice ads listed 8:00 PM shows for the run, billed as featuring NRPS [2]
- Reviewer rates this the best show of the Capitol run, and pairs it with 6-24-70 for Jerry's evident enjoyment [6]
- Called the last truly great Pigpen show [8]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-11-06.aud.warner.17183.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Ken Leigh and Dave Tamarkin; transferred by Jack Warner; source: Audience [1]. Also: Reviewer's own tape supplies a song and a half that Ken Leigh's recording missed; Reviewer notes the first half apparently comes from a different source [9][13]
- **gd70-11-06.d3new.hanno.19922.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Marty Weinberg; transferred by Uli Teute and Hanno Bunjes; source: Audience - Improved Disc 3 Only [3]
- **gd1970-11-06.aud.weinberg.moore-berger.119818.flac16**: taped by Jerry Moore and Marty Weinberg; transferred by Rob Berger; source: partial: aud reel master > reel, Jerry Moore's copy of Marty Weinberg's master; [4]. Also: Only complete copy is shn 17183, Jack Warner's composite of Ken Lee and Dave Tamarkin cassette recordings [4]
- **gd1970-11-06.aud.evans.3338.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Teddy Goodbear; source: Audience [2]
